query: How do review facets differ by sentiment label?

per_column.name: product_performance_state
per_column.rationale: Clean ordinal-like categories (works_as_intended / partially_works / does_not_work) that are external to the sentiment label and can be cross-tabulated against label_pos to reveal how functional outcomes relate to positive vs negative sentiment.

per_column.name: defect_or_failure_present
per_column.rationale: Well-separated interpretable categories describing failure modes, dominated by 'not_present' but with meaningful defect subtypes. Segmentable and comparable against sentiment; an associational variable, not a restatement.

per_column.name: expectation_met_or_exceeded
per_column.rationale: Interpretable categories capturing expectation fulfilment. While closely coupled with sentiment, it adds a distinct explanatory dimension (e.g. misled_by_advertising vs simple disappointment) and supports meaningful grouping against the focus.

per_column.name: primary_attribute_type
per_column.rationale: Facet taxonomy (functionality, quality, ease_of_use, price_or_value, etc.) that is exactly the 'review facet' dimension the query targets. Interpretable categories, though a few (comfort_or_fit, performance_speed) are near-empty and weaken some cells.

judge.rationale: All four added columns are external, interpretable categorical variables with well-separated categories that can be segmented and cross-tabulated against label_pos, directly serving the query about how review facets differ by sentiment. None merely restate the label as an opaque score. Minor weaknesses: expectation_met_or_exceeded is somewhat semantically entangled with sentiment (borderline near-restatement of valence), and primary_attribute_type has a long tail of near-constant categories that yield thin comparison cells. Overall a strong, informative set for exploratory analysis.
